idea: An inventory service: reserving stock lets orders go through when exactly zero is left, and restocking a product resets its reserved count.
A bank ledger in integer cents: interest and fee calculations come out wrong for some accounts (int vs float division, rounding), and the monthly statement total ignores the last transaction.
A meeting-room booking service: back-to-back bookings are rejected as overlapping and a booking ending at midnight is lost; booking times are datetime objects.
An in-memory LRU cache used by a product catalogue API: get() doesn't refresh recency, and the default tags list is shared between cache entries (mutable default argument).
A CSV sales-report generator (csv module on strings): grouping by region is case-sensitive so 'EU' and 'eu' are split, and the report's top seller is the lowest instead of highest.
A sliding-window API rate limiter keyed by user: requests exactly at the window edge are counted twice, and different users share one bucket because of a wrong dict key.
A paginated REST-style handler over a list of records: page 1 skips the first page_size items, and the has_next flag is wrong on the last full page.
An event scheduler that sorts and filters events: dates stored as 'D/M/YYYY' strings are compared as strings so ordering is wrong, and filtering 'upcoming' events drops the ones today.

A retry helper with exponential backoff used by a payments client (the sleep function is injected so tests don't wait): the delay grows wrong, retries exceed max_attempts by one, and a non-retryable error is silently swallowed and returns None.

A package dependency resolver (install order via DFS): diamond dependencies are falsely reported as cycles (visited vs on-stack confusion), and the install order puts a package before one of its dependencies.

A pricing service with a memoised price lookup: the cache key ignores the currency so EUR prices leak into USD answers, and a percentage discount is applied twice when a coupon is combined with a sale.

A tiny expression evaluator for spreadsheet-style formulas (tokenizer, parser, evaluator in separate files): subtraction is right-associative, negative numbers after an operator fail to parse, and cell references in lowercase aren't resolved.
A todo-list library (models, storage, query helpers): add priorities with stable sorting by priority then due date, and filtering by multiple tags (all-of / any-of).
A library lending system: add a reservation queue (holds) so a returned book goes to the first person waiting, with hold expiry after 3 days.
A shopping cart with line items and tax: add discount codes (percentage, fixed amount, buy-one-get-one on a SKU) with rules for which ones stack.
A URL shortener (id encoding, storage, service): add custom aliases with validation and link expiry with an injected clock.
A parking-lot system with spot types: add EV charging spots and hourly pricing with a daily cap per vehicle type.
A web-server access-log analyzer (parsing, aggregation): add per-endpoint p50/p95/p99 latency and an error-rate report sorted by worst endpoint.
A task runner that executes jobs in insertion order: add job dependencies with a valid execution order, cycle detection with a clear error naming the cycle, and skipping dependents of failed jobs.
An in-memory key-value store with get/set/delete: add nested transactions (begin, rollback, commit) where rollback undoes only the innermost transaction.

A maze solver: a grid parser, a Maze model and a solver stub. Stage 1 fix a parser bug with row/column order. Stage 2 implement the shortest path through a maze with keys (lowercase) and doors (uppercase) and print the path. Stage 3 large mazes must be fast (BFS over position+keys bitmask).

A friend-recommendation service over a social graph loaded from edge lists. Stage 1 fix the loader so friendships are mutual. Stage 2 recommend the top-k non-friends ranked by mutual friends (ties by id). Stage 3 make it fast for 10^5 users.

A word-game helper: Stage 1 fix the bitmask helper for letters. Stage 2 find the maximum total length of words with all distinct characters (no letter repeated across chosen words). Stage 3 make it fast on large word lists (dedupe masks, prune).

A card game engine (deck, card parsing, rules): Stage 1 fix the card-value parser for face cards. Stage 2 find whether any three cards in a hand sum to 15 and return them. Stage 3 count all such triples fast for large hands (counting by value).

A delivery-route planner over a road network: Stage 1 fix the distance unit bug in the graph builder. Stage 2 implement the shortest delivery time between two depots. Stage 3 make it fast for large networks (Dijkstra with a heap instead of a linear scan).

A search autocomplete service: Stage 1 fix query normalisation (case and whitespace). Stage 2 return the top-k completions for a prefix by frequency, ties alphabetical. Stage 3 make it fast for 10^5 phrases and many queries (a trie with cached top-k).
